origins.section: Spot the Problem: A Field Read Before Its Initializer Sees Its Default
Spot the Problem: A Field Read Before Its Initializer Sees Its Default
An Inner Class's Instance Holds Its Outer Object; a Static Nested Class's Doesn't
A File Has at Most One Public Top-Level Class, and the File Is Named After It

gates.says: all 4 of this quiz's answerable readings held and each was taken over the question as it stands

recorded.prompt:q-capacity-before-factor: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-capacity-before-factor: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-capacity-before-factor: Page decides b: 'javac copies the field initializers ... in source order'; 'Until its initializer runs, a field holds its default: null, 0 or false'; Endpoint example: 'url is initialized first, while host is still null ... javac doesn't follow method calls'; 'An initializer that calls a method is never constant' (so Integer.getInteger is not inlined, unlike port).
recorded.prompt:q-caption-from-super: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-caption-from-super: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-caption-from-super: Page decides c: 'A superclass constructor runs before all of this, so an overridden method it calls sees the same defaults' (Handler/OrderHandler prints [/null/orders]); 'port is right because it is a constant variable (final, primitive or String, constant initializer), and javac inlines 8443 at every read. An initializer that calls a method is never constant.' text = "Save" is a constant variable and gets inlined. tooltip calls System.getProperty, so it is not constant and is still null.
recorded.prompt:q-listener-on-static-bus: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-listener-on-static-bus: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-listener-on-static-bus: Page decides a: 'javac 21 adds the field only to an inner or anonymous class that uses its outer instance (reads its fields or calls its instance methods)'; 'A listener registered on a static registry pins its outer object the same way.' Reference: 'anonymous class in an instance method | this$0 only if it uses the outer instance'.
recorded.prompt:q-fee-schedule-file: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-fee-schedule-file: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-fee-schedule-file: Page decides b with a matching example: with TaxTable package-private inside Invoice.java, 'javac Checkout.java on a clean checkout' gives 'error: cannot find symbol'; 'javac finds a type it hasn't compiled by its name: it looks for TaxTable.class or TaxTable.java on the class path (here the current directory)'. Small gap: the page's files sit 'in the same package', while the stem says 'no package'. The page never mentions the unnamed package, but the current-directory class-path lookup covers this case.

recorded.prompt:q-capacity-before-factor:a: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-capacity-before-factor:a: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-capacity-before-factor:a: Refuted: initializers run 'in source order'; the Endpoint example shows a field read via a method before its initializer ran sees its default ('https://null:8443').
recorded.prompt:q-capacity-before-factor:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-capacity-before-factor:c: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-capacity-before-factor:c: Refuted: 'Naming host directly there is an illegal forward reference, but javac doesn't follow method calls.' The Endpoint example compiles and runs.
recorded.prompt:q-capacity-before-factor:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-capacity-before-factor:d: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-capacity-before-factor:d: Refuted: 'Until its initializer runs, a field holds its default: null, 0 or false'. An int reads 0; the Endpoint example reads an uninitialized field without throwing. The page never says outright that nothing throws, but this follows from the default-value rule.

recorded.prompt:q-listener-on-static-bus:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-listener-on-static-bus:b: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-listener-on-static-bus:b: Refuted: 'uses its outer instance (reads its fields or calls its instance methods)'. Calling redraw() counts, so the listener gets this$0.
recorded.prompt:q-listener-on-static-bus:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-listener-on-static-bus:c: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-listener-on-static-bus:c: Refuted: 'A listener registered on a static registry pins its outer object'. The dashboard stays reachable through the listener's this$0, the same way 'The cached row keeps the report's 50 MB reachable'.
recorded.prompt:q-listener-on-static-bus:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-listener-on-static-bus:d: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-listener-on-static-bus:d: Refuted: the static registry keeps the listener, which 'pins its outer object'. Report example: the row outlives the dropped report variable ('report collected: false'). The page does not say outright that the reference never runs outer-to-inner, but its claim that the inner object holds the outer is enough to refute d.
